definitions.policy: These are research records about restriction, survival, reconstruction, and authenticity. They are not catalog TextRecord editions. Atlas never fabricates missing passages, hypothetical quotations, or substitute artifacts, and it keeps physical evidence separate from claimed authorship and provenance.

restrictionTypes.canon-excluded: Outside a stated canon boundary; this alone is not a ban.
restrictionTypes.ecclesiastically-prohibited: Prohibited by a named religious authority in a documented place and period.
restrictionTypes.state-banned: Prohibited by a named government or state authority.
restrictionTypes.censored: Publication, import, circulation, or access was officially constrained.
restrictionTypes.destroyed: Copies or a corpus were deliberately destroyed by a documented authority or actor.
restrictionTypes.restricted-to-qualified-audience: Teaching or exposition was limited by audience qualification; this is not automatically a whole-work ban.
restrictionTypes.blasphemy-restriction: Restricted under a blasphemy rule or offense.
restrictionTypes.obscenity-restriction: Restricted under an obscenity or public-morals rule.
restrictionTypes.political-religious-suppression: Suppression combined political control with regulation of a religious community or practice.

survivalStatuses.LOST: Known from references or quotations, but no direct manuscript of the work survives.
survivalStatuses.INDIRECTLY_ATTESTED: Known principally through another writer, catalog, epitome, or quotation chain.
survivalStatuses.FRAGMENTARY: Direct fragments survive; gaps must remain visible and cannot be filled as primary text.
survivalStatuses.DISPUTED_LOST_WORK: Later sources allege a lost work, but its earlier existence or form remains disputed.

authenticityStatuses.DEMONSTRATED_MODERN_FORGERY: Evidence establishes modern creation despite an older attribution.
authenticityStatuses.MODERN_FORGERY_OR_HOAX: Scholarship identifies a modern creation whose initial or later presentation involved hoax claims.
authenticityStatuses.MODERN_FORGERY: Scholarship rejects the claimed antiquity and identifies modern manufacture.
authenticityStatuses.DEMONSTRATED_HOAX: The makers or evidence establish deliberate deceptive manufacture.
authenticityStatuses.SUSPECTED_FORGERY_DISPUTED: The majority view favors forgery, while a documented minority disputes that conclusion.

suppressionEvents.title: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium — 1616 restriction
suppressionEvents.headline: Ecclesiastical prohibition — historical restriction
suppressionEvents.summary: The Congregation of the Index suspended Copernicus's work until correction in the 1616 decree. The Index ceased to carry ecclesiastical-law force in 1966.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
suppressionEvents.jurisdiction: Rome and jurisdictions applying the Roman Index
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: The Index ceased to have the force of ecclesiastical law under the 14 June 1966 notification.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: The decree treated the work's heliocentric teaching as contrary to Scripture and suspended it until correction.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: No current Index prohibition with force of ecclesiastical law; the 1966 notification retained a general moral admonition concerning writings that endanger faith or morals.

suppressionEvents.title: Foscarini's Letter on the Pythagorean and Copernican Opinion — 1616 prohibition
suppressionEvents.headline: Ecclesiastical prohibition — historical restriction
suppressionEvents.summary: The 1616 Index decree prohibited Paolo Antonio Foscarini's defense of reconciling Copernicanism with Scripture.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
suppressionEvents.jurisdiction: Rome and jurisdictions applying the Roman Index
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: The Index ceased to have the force of ecclesiastical law under the 14 June 1966 notification.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: The decree prohibited Foscarini's work in the context of judging heliocentric claims contrary to Scripture.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Historical prohibition; no current Index prohibition with force of ecclesiastical law.

suppressionEvents.title: Tyndale New Testament — suppression and destruction
suppressionEvents.headline: Banned translation — copies were destroyed
suppressionEvents.summary: Tyndale's English New Testament was printed abroad, smuggled into England, officially suppressed, and publicly burned; only a small number of copies of the first edition survive.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: Historical and inactive; later English Bible publication followed different legal and ecclesiastical regimes.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: An unauthorized vernacular translation was treated as religiously and politically impermissible.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Historical suppression only; surviving copies are held and displayed by research libraries.

suppressionEvents.title: Watchtower and Golden Age literature — German bans and seizures
suppressionEvents.headline: Political-religious suppression by state authorities
suppressionEvents.summary: German jurisdictions and Nazi authorities banned organizations and seized Jehovah's Witness literature as pressure intensified in 1933.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
suppressionEvents.authority: German state and Nazi authorities, with measures varying by jurisdiction
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: Historical Nazi-era suppression; no current German restriction is asserted by this record.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: Authorities portrayed proselytizing and refusal of state loyalty, military service, or Nazi practices as subversive.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Historical suppression record; current access is outside the scope of the cited historical source.

suppressionEvents.title: Maya books destroyed in Yucatán under Diego de Landa
suppressionEvents.headline: Destroyed corpus — surviving contents cannot be invented
suppressionEvents.summary: Library of Congress reporting describes Diego de Landa's destruction of Maya books in Yucatán beginning in 1562. This is a corpus-level event, not an invented title, a more precise location claim, or a claim that all Maya books were destroyed.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
culturalRestrictions: Treat Maya knowledge as living cultural heritage and do not synthesize replacement books.
safetyNotes: Colonial descriptions such as 'devil worship' are attributed to suppressors, not adopted as neutral descriptions.
suppressionEvents.authority: Diego de Landa and Franciscan authorities
suppressionEvents.jurisdiction: Yucatán; the cited source does not establish a more precise event location
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: The destruction is irreversible; this record does not assert a continuing legal ban.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: The suppressors characterized Maya religious books and practices as idolatrous or demonic.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Historical destruction event; surviving Maya manuscripts and living traditions must be documented independently.

suppressionEvents.title: Zhuan Falun — PRC publication restriction
suppressionEvents.headline: State restriction — current status bounded by source dates
suppressionEvents.summary: Commission testimony reports that Zhuan Falun was taken out of print in 1996; later government reporting documents confiscation and suppression of Falun Gong materials.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Copyrighted modern work. Metadata and outbound evidence links only; no full text or extended excerpts.
safetyNotes: Claims are attributed to their government or witness source and are not silently updated beyond the source period.
suppressionEvents.authority: People's Republic of China publishing and security authorities
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: Not established by the cited sources.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: Official action formed part of broader state control of Falun Gong publication and practice; exact rationales vary by order and source.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Restrictions are documented through the latest cited historical reporting; post-2009 legal status is not independently verified in this record.

suppressionEvents.title: Shepherd of Hermas in Codex Sinaiticus
suppressionEvents.headline: Canon boundary — not a ban
suppressionEvents.summary: Codex Sinaiticus preserves the Shepherd after the New Testament sequence, evidence of early collection boundaries and use. Canon status must be stated by community and period; exclusion from a later canon is not prohibition.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
suppressionEvents.authority: No banning authority; the Codex Sinaiticus manuscript arrangement is the evidence
suppressionEvents.jurisdiction: Specific fourth-century manuscript context; later canon boundaries vary by community
suppressionEvents.restrictionDate: Fourth century manuscript context; no prohibition date
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: No prohibition reason exists; this is a canon-boundary control record.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Not treated as a ban. Present-day canonical reception must be described tradition by tradition.

suppressionEvents.title: Mishnah Hagigah 2:1 — audience limits on exposition
suppressionEvents.dateLabel: Mishnah compiled around the early third century CE
suppressionEvents.statusLabel: AUDIENCE-RESTRICTED TEACHING — NOT A BOOK BAN
suppressionEvents.headline: Qualified-audience restriction — possession is not prohibited
suppressionEvents.summary: Mishnah Hagigah 2:1 limits exposition of creation and chariot subjects according to audience and qualification. It does not prohibit possessing or reading the Mishnah as a whole.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
culturalRestrictions: Do not generalize this historical textual rule into a uniform present-day Jewish access policy.
suppressionEvents.authority: Rabbinic norm recorded in Mishnah Hagigah 2:1
suppressionEvents.jurisdiction: Rabbinic teaching context represented by the Mishnah
suppressionEvents.restrictionDate: Mishnaic period; the passage does not supply a modern enforcement date
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: Current application varies and is not established by this record.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: The passage ties exposition of specified subjects to audience size and demonstrated understanding.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Historical teaching restriction; not a whole-work ban and not a claim of universal current practice.

suppressionEvents.title: The Love That Dares to Speak Its Name — blasphemous-libel prosecution
suppressionEvents.headline: Blasphemy prosecution — historical legal restriction
suppressionEvents.summary: Publication of James Kirkup's poem led to a blasphemous-libel conviction. The common-law offenses of blasphemy and blasphemous libel were abolished in England and Wales in 2008.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Copyrighted modern poem. Metadata and legal history only; the poem is not reproduced.
safetyNotes: Do not reproduce sexually explicit text in summaries or search snippets.
suppressionEvents.authority: English criminal courts; conviction followed a private prosecution
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: Publication was prosecuted as blasphemous libel under the law then in force.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: The relevant common-law offenses were abolished in England and Wales in 2008.

suppressionEvents.title: Kama Sutra — 1965 Portuguese censorship episode
suppressionEvents.headline: Obscenity restriction — exact rescission date unverified
suppressionEvents.summary: Cambridge University Library records that a Portuguese edition of the Kama Sutra was swiftly banned under the Estado Novo censorship environment in 1965.
suppressionEvents.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
safetyNotes: Treat the work as a Sanskrit cultural and literary text; do not automatically label it scripture.
suppressionEvents.authority: Estado Novo censorship apparatus; the cited source does not identify the precise order-issuing office
suppressionEvents.restrictionEnd: Exact rescission date not established by the cited source.
suppressionEvents.reasonAsStated: The episode occurred within state censorship of erotic or allegedly pornographic publication.
suppressionEvents.currentStatus: Historical restriction; exact rescission date remains unverified in this record.

hypotheticalSources.title: Q source
hypotheticalSources.dateLabel: Modern scholarly hypothesis concerning first-century Gospel relationships
hypotheticalSources.headline: Hypothetical Q Source
hypotheticalSources.summary: Q is a scholarly source hypothesis used to explain material shared by Matthew and Luke but absent from Mark. No Q manuscript has been found.
hypotheticalSources.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
hypotheticalSources.proposedEntity: A proposed sayings or source collection used in the composition of Matthew and Luke
argumentsFor: Substantial shared Matthew-Luke material is absent from Mark.
Patterns of wording and sequence can be modeled through a shared source.
argumentsAgainst: Direct literary dependence models can explain the same data without Q.
There is no physical witness and no universally agreed reconstruction.
hypotheticalSources.currentAssessment: Q remains influential but contested; reconstructions are models of Gospel relationships, not recovered documents.
hypotheticalSources.modelBoundary: Never create a manuscript, inventory number, edition, quotation, or first-person voice for Q.

hypotheticalSources.title: Pentateuchal source models
hypotheticalSources.headline: Reconstructed strata — not recovered scrolls
hypotheticalSources.summary: J, E, P, D and later supplementary or fragmentary models infer compositional layers from the received Pentateuch. Scholars disagree over source boundaries and whether each model represents an independent document.
hypotheticalSources.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
hypotheticalSources.proposedEntity: Proposed source strata and editorial stages within the Pentateuch
argumentsFor: Repetitions, narrative tensions, vocabulary, and style support compositional differentiation.
Some legal and narrative groupings show internally coherent patterns.
argumentsAgainst: Competing documentary, supplementary, and fragmentary models divide the evidence differently.
No manuscript labeled J, E, P, or D survives as a separate source document.
hypotheticalSources.currentAssessment: Source analysis remains a family of debated models rather than a single recovered textual history.
hypotheticalSources.modelBoundary: Do not turn sigla into physical works, assign unsupported exact dates, or synthesize continuous source texts.

hypotheticalSources.title: Deuteronomistic History
hypotheticalSources.dateLabel: Modern hypothesis concerning Deuteronomy through Kings
hypotheticalSources.headline: Shared editorial patterns — no recovered master manuscript
hypotheticalSources.summary: The Deuteronomistic History proposes editorial unity across Deuteronomy through Kings. The model has influential variants and substantial challenges.
hypotheticalSources.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
hypotheticalSources.proposedEntity: A proposed editorial work or process linking Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, Samuel, and Kings
argumentsFor: Recurring language, covenant themes, and evaluations of kings support shared editorial activity.
Some historical and theological patterns span the proposed corpus.
argumentsAgainst: Block, library, and multiple-redaction models explain the corpus without one unified history.
The scale, date, and number of editorial layers remain disputed.
hypotheticalSources.currentAssessment: The construct remains important but is neither a physical manuscript nor a consensus single-author work.
hypotheticalSources.modelBoundary: Represent model variants and evidence, not a fabricated Deuteronomistic book.

hypotheticalSources.title: Proto-Indo-European religious reconstruction
hypotheticalSources.dateLabel: Modern reconstruction of prehistoric linguistic and cultural evidence
hypotheticalSources.headline: Comparative reconstruction — no unitary scripture
hypotheticalSources.summary: Comparative linguistics and mythology support a limited set of inherited terms and patterns, while many proposed deities and narratives remain doubtful.
hypotheticalSources.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
hypotheticalSources.proposedEntity: Selected inherited religious vocabulary, formulae, and cultural patterns
argumentsFor: Regular linguistic cognates can support inherited names or concepts.
Some poetic and ritual formulas recur across separated Indo-European traditions.
argumentsAgainst: Contact, convergence, semantic change, and chance resemblance complicate comparisons.
The evidence does not recover a complete or uniform religion.
hypotheticalSources.currentAssessment: Only bounded, method-specific reconstructions should be presented; confidence varies term by term.
hypotheticalSources.modelBoundary: Never create a Proto-Indo-European scripture, canonical narrative, or verbatim prayer.

hypotheticalSources.title: Proto-Indo-Iranian religious reconstruction
hypotheticalSources.dateLabel: Modern reconstruction from Vedic and Avestan evidence
hypotheticalSources.headline: Recoverable elements — not a complete religious system
hypotheticalSources.summary: Vedic and Avestan correspondences support reconstruction of some inherited vocabulary, deities, and ritual concepts, but not a complete organic system.
hypotheticalSources.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
argumentsFor: Systematic Vedic-Avestan correspondences support shared inherited elements.
Related ritual and poetic terminology can be compared historically.
argumentsAgainst: Later developments differ sharply and cannot be projected wholesale backward.
The cited scholarship cautions that an organic complete system cannot be reconstructed.
hypotheticalSources.currentAssessment: A bounded comparative reconstruction is possible for selected features only.
hypotheticalSources.modelBoundary: Do not merge later Vedic and Zoroastrian traditions or generate a proto-canon.

hypotheticalSources.title: Rigvedic oral compositional history
hypotheticalSources.dateLabel: Modern reconstruction of ancient oral composition and transmission
hypotheticalSources.headline: Oral history model — not a lost predecessor book
hypotheticalSources.summary: Formulaic reuse, poet lineages, arrangement, and preservation practices support models of Rigvedic oral composition. Exact early stages and dates remain uncertain.
hypotheticalSources.rightsStatus: Metadata and original neutral summary only. Edition, translation, image, and facsimile rights require separate review.
hypotheticalSources.proposedEntity: Stages and practices in the oral composition and preservation of the Rigveda
argumentsFor: Formulaic language, reuse, and lineage organization provide internal evidence.
Highly controlled oral preservation explains later textual stability.
argumentsAgainst: No contemporary manuscript witnesses the earliest compositional stages.
Oral development cannot be reduced to one lost written archetype.
hypotheticalSources.currentAssessment: Scholarship can model oral composition and transmission without manufacturing an earlier canonical text.
hypotheticalSources.modelBoundary: Do not synthesize a false canonical oral version or present reconstructed stages as verbatim quotations.

disputedWorks.headline: Modern forgery — ancient papyrus does not date the writing
disputedWorks.summary: Material testing initially left open the possibility of an old papyrus support, but textual dependence on a modern online Gospel of Thomas edition and provenance failures establish modern composition.
disputedWorks.rightsStatus: Metadata and evidence summaries only. Images, transcriptions, editions, and facsimiles require separate rights review.
safetyNotes: Do not repeat sensational claims about Jesus or early Christianity as established history.

disputedWorks.claimedAuthorship: Presented as an otherwise unknown early Christian gospel witness
disputedWorks.physicalDate: Papyrus support may be ancient; that result does not date the inscription

evidenceFor.claim: Radiocarbon and ink reporting initially did not prove that the support or ink was modern.

evidenceAgainst.claim: Textual correspondences include dependence on a modern online Gospel of Thomas edition and its error.
The ownership and acquisition account lacks secure independent provenance.
